changeSet.sql:
-- A permission's dictionary entry determines its scope. Position grants may -- now carry either scope, while the composite FK still rejects mismatches. ALTER TABLE identity.position_permission DROP CONSTRAINT position_permission_scope_check, ADD CONSTRAINT position_permission_scope_check CHECK (scope IN ('BRANCH', 'BUSINESS'));
-- Preserve direct grants only when the position is already exclusive to staff -- holding the same grant. A shared position must not widen authority silently. INSERT INTO identity.position_permission(position_id, business_id, permission_code, scope) SELECT DISTINCT a.position_id, a.business_id, g.permission_code, 'BUSINESS' FROM identity.staff_business_permission g JOIN identity.staff_branch_position a ON a.staff_id = g.staff_id AND a.business_id = g.business_id AND a.revoked_at IS NULL AND a.assigned_at <= clock_timestamp() JOIN identity.position p ON p.position_id = a.position_id AND p.business_id = a.business_id AND p.is_active WHERE g.revoked_at IS NULL AND g.granted_at <= clock_timestamp() AND NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM identity.staff_branch_position x WHERE x.position_id = a.position_id AND x.business_id = a.business_id AND x.revoked_at IS NULL AND NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM identity.staff_business_permission gx WHERE gx.staff_id = x.staff_id AND gx.business_id = x.business_id AND gx.permission_code = g.permission_code AND gx.revoked_at IS NULL AND gx.granted_at <= clock_timestamp() ) ) ON CONFLICT (position_id, permission_code) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL DO NOTHING;
